title: Objectwise tensoring preserves sheafification-isomorphisms
statement:
In the situation of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf], let $a$ be sheafification of
$\mathcal A$-valued presheaves on $C$, left adjoint to the inclusion $\Sh(C,\mathcal A)\subseteq\mathrm{PSh}(C,\mathcal A)$,
and let $W$ be the class of morphisms $g$ of presheaves with $a(g)$ invertible. Equivalently, $g\in W$ if and only if
$\Hom(g,H)$ is bijective for every sheaf $H$.

1. If $g\in W$ and $F$ is a presheaf, then $F\otimes_pg\in W$ and $g\otimes_pF\in W$.
2. If $g\colon F\to F'$ and $h\colon G\to G'$ lie in $W$, then $g\otimes_ph\in W$.
3. For presheaves $F,G$, the morphism $F\otimes_pG\to aF\otimes_paG$ built from the units of
   $a$ lies in $W$; hence $a(F\otimes_pG)\to a(aF\otimes_paG)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $g:P\to Q$ and $u=a(g):aP\to aQ$. For each sheaf $H$, the sheafification adjunction identifies the precomposition map $g^*:\Hom(Q,H)\to\Hom(P,H)$ with $u^*:\Hom(aQ,H)\to\Hom(aP,H)$. If $u$ is invertible then all these maps are bijective. Conversely, assume they are bijective. Taking $H=aP$, surjectivity supplies $v:aQ\to aP$ with $v\circ u=1_{aP}$. Taking $H=aQ$, injectivity and $(u\circ v)\circ u=u=1_{aQ}\circ u$ give $u\circ v=1_{aQ}$. Thus $u$ is invertible, proving the characterization of $W$.

source.place: The equivalence of the two descriptions of W

proof.text: Let $g:P\to Q$ lie in $W$, and let $H$ be a sheaf. The natural tensor--internal-hom adjunction of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf] identifies precomposition by $F\otimes_p g$ on maps to $H$ with precomposition by $g$ on maps to $[F,H]$. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-hom-sheaf], $[F,H]$ is a sheaf, so the latter map is bijective. Step 1 gives $F\otimes_p g\in W$. Write $c_{P,F}:P\otimes_pF\to F\otimes_pP$ for the objectwise symmetry from [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf]. Its naturality gives $g\otimes_pF=c_{Q,F}^{-1}\circ(F\otimes_pg)\circ c_{P,F}$. Applying $a$ expresses $a(g\otimes_pF)$ as a composite of isomorphisms, proving $g\otimes_pF\in W$.

For $g:F\to F\prime$ and $h:G\to G\prime$ in $W$, functoriality of the objectwise tensor gives $g\otimes_ph=(F\prime\otimes_ph)\circ(g\otimes_pG)$. Both factors lie in $W$ by clause 1. Since $a$ is a functor, it sends this composite to the composite of the two isomorphisms $a$ supplies, so $W$ is closed under composition and $g\otimes_ph\in W$.

For each presheaf $F$ and each sheaf $H$, the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] states precisely that precomposition with the unit $\eta_F:F\to aF$ gives a bijection $\Hom(aF,H)\to\Hom(F,H)$. Step 1 therefore gives $\eta_F\in W$, and the same argument with $G$ gives $\eta_G\in W$. Clause 2 applied to these units shows that $\eta_F\otimes_p\eta_G:F\otimes_pG\to aF\otimes_paG$ lies in $W$. By definition of $W$, its sheafification $a(F\otimes_pG)\to a(aF\otimes_paG)$ is an isomorphism.
